objective: Sum decimal digits arithmetically over the whole nonnegative safe-integer Number domain.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Remainder and Number safe-integer bounds remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: The digit calculation is mainly an arithmetic exercise.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Repeated quotient reduction transfers to numeric algorithms.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: One bounded while loop fits the foundation stage.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: An explicit safe domain avoids precision and exponential-text ambiguities.

defects: Unbounded whole-number wording allowed unsafe Number inputs.
A six-digit-only shortcut passed all original cases.
The logarithmic magnitude-versus-digit input model was unstated.
rationale: Define Number input from zero through MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, with no strings/BigInts/validation requirement. Add the actual maximum, a near-maximum repeated-digit input, large powers and mixed zero digits. Expected sums come from exact decimal digits. Original reference/junior/senior and an arithmetic do-while alternative pass. The authored O(log n) target is in numeric magnitude, equivalently O(d) decimal digits; zero is constant work. Unknown static estimates remain unpenalized.

objective: Count inclusive integer multiples across signed bounded endpoints using a positive divisor.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Integer range iteration and remainder remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Inclusive bounded counting is a practical aggregation pattern.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Signed endpoints and zero transfer to other range algorithms.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A basic for scan is suitable for the stated tier.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Positive-divisor and span bounds prevent invalid or unbounded stepping.

defects: A zero or negative divisor was not excluded although the senior increment assumed a positive one.
Ignoring all negative multiples passed original examples.
The complexity-label n could be confused with the divisor argument.
rationale: Require divisor 1..1000000 and integer endpoints -10000..10000, preserving inclusive endpoints, zero and reversed-empty ranges. Test negative-only and crossing-zero intervals, the maximal 20001 positions, large divisor, missing singleton, signed zero and reversed negative endpoints. Explain that the teaching target's n is visited range length rather than the divisor parameter. A faster closed-form alternative remains accepted with base 25 XP; no method-source heuristic is introduced.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Queue operations and exact removed values are practical.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Falsy values and object identity transfer to other collection APIs.

relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Mutation/identity fixtures prevent silent value substitution.

defects: The name-only wording conflicted with the existing numeric case and omitted other valid values.
Falsy fallback and cloned served objects passed the original fixtures.
The senior empty fast path obscured the requested push-then-shift demonstration.
rationale: Define an ordinary dense mutable queue through 10000 JavaScript values, preserving original-array mutation, surviving order and object references. Add false/zero/empty-string/undefined/null, frozen item objects, identical-looking distinct references, an empty object newcomer and the upper bound. Remove the senior empty shortcut so all revealed forms demonstrate the stated operations. Time is O(n) in the dense-array element-moving model, explicitly not a fixed engine timing guarantee; extra space is not separately graded.
